title: Tone Keyboard
description: Three force sensors are keys: press one and the buzzer plays its note.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 3 × force sensor (FSR), 3 × 10 kΩ resistor, 1 × piezo buzzer, and some jumper wires.
Push the force sensor in, its two legs in two different columns.
steps.goal: Put the force sensor on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One leg of the force sensor → that same row.
steps.goal: Connect one leg of the force sensor to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the force sensor's other leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
steps.goal: Connect the force sensor's other leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as the pin A0 wire, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: The force sensor and this resistor share the 5 V between them — so the pin's voltage changes as the force sensor does.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor next to the pin A0 wire.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. That resistor's other leg → that same row.
hints: Now the reading goes up when the pad is pressed.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push a second force sensor in, its two legs in two different columns.
steps.goal: Put the second force sensor on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the second force sensor to the red + row.
steps.goal: Connect one leg of the second force sensor to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second force sensor's other leg to pin A1 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A1 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
steps.goal: Connect the second force sensor's other leg to pin A1.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as the pin A1 wire, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: The force sensor and this resistor share the 5 V between them — so the pin's voltage changes as the force sensor does.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor next to the pin A1 wire.

steps.clip: Run a wire from that resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the reading goes up when the pad is pressed.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push a third force sensor in, its two legs in two different columns.
steps.goal: Put the third force sensor on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the third force sensor to the red + row.
steps.goal: Connect one leg of the third force sensor to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the third force sensor's other leg to pin A2 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A2 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
steps.goal: Connect the third force sensor's other leg to pin A2.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as the pin A2 wire, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: The force sensor and this resistor share the 5 V between them — so the pin's voltage changes as the force sensor does.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor next to the pin A2 wire.

steps.clip: Run a wire from that resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the reading goes up when the pad is pressed.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push the buzzer in, its two legs in two different columns.
hints: The + leg is marked on top (and is usually longer).
It only works one way round.
steps.goal: Put the buzzer on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the buzzer's + leg to pin 8 on the Arduino.
hints: tone() on this pin makes the buzzer sing.
steps.goal: Connect the buzzer's + leg to pin 8.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the buzzer's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the buzzer's − leg to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Press each force sensor: each one plays its own note.
